solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Bike lay idle

definitions.meaning: a small motorised two-wheeler with pedals
to have ... about is to have mooched listlessly, doing nothing

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a light motorcycle with pedals, and the past tense of a verb for sulking about doing nothing.

clue.text: Blondie's agent for each song obtains unknown bit of income

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per head'

indicators.note: the song gets hold of the following letters, so they go inside it

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem or song
X is the classic algebraic unknown

indicators.note: only a bit of the word income is used: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A singer with Blondie gets a royalty from a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blondie' looks like the band; here it is any bleached blonde. 'obtains' puts X plus I inside ODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen peroxide is the bleaching chemical used to make hair platinum, so it is what makes a blondie.

clue.text: Repellent master circles compound for ages

indicators.note: the reversed master goes round the compound's letters
something repellent pushes back, so the word for master is driven backwards

parts.note: sir is a schoolboy's word for his master
a pen is an enclosure or compound for animals

explanation.surface: An insect repellent's chief chemical surrounds a compound that lasts for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repellent' looks like an adjective or a bug spray, but it is the reversal signal: it drives the schoolboy's word for master backwards. 'circles' then wraps that round the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe maturing over time, as fruit or cheese mellows with age.

clue.text: Electronic payment system set up for blackleg

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised, so read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: BACS is the UK's Bankers' Automated Clearing Services, which moves salaries electronically

explanation.surface: An electronic payroll system was arranged to pay a strike-breaker.
explanation.walkthrough: BACS, the British system that pays wages straight into bank accounts, is turned upside down by 'set up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British words for a worker who crosses a picket line during a strike.

clue.text: Perennial trouble experienced in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so in a down clue the joined pieces read upwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
had means experienced, as in 'had a fright'

explanation.surface: Someone suffers ongoing trouble after they retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perennial' looks like an adjective meaning constant; it is a noun, a plant. 'in retirement' turns AILHAD round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuberous garden flower that returns year after year is an example of a perennial plant.

clue.text: PM — not working. AM — acting with new film crew member

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the letters for working from the surname

parts.note: David Cameron was British Prime Minister when this puzzle appeared in 2010
on means working, as a machine that is switched on
A is a standard abbreviation for acting, as in an acting rank

explanation.surface: A news report: the Prime Minister is off duty, and the morning sees an actor with a new film crew member.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2010 Prime Minister, David Cameron, loses ON to give CAMER; AM is written as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: The person operating the camera on a shoot is part of the film crew.

clue.text: Fluttering, one chirps, soft to loud?

definitions.text: Fluttering, one chirps, soft to loud?

indicators.note: fluttering suggests letters flapping about into a new order
the soft letter changes to the loud letter in the fodder

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
f (forte) is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A bird flutters and chirps, its song swelling from quiet to loud.
explanation.walkthrough: Change P to F in ONECHIRPS, then 'Fluttering' rearranges the letters. The whole clue also describes the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink-red finch is a small songbird, which flutters about and chirps.

clue.text: Burns evident, with afternoon temperature somewhere around 34º

parts.note: Rab is the Scots short form of Robert, as in Rabbie Burns the poet
A is taken here as an abbreviation for afternoon

explanation.surface: Sunburn shows after an afternoon in a temperature of about 34 degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' looks like sunburn but is the Scottish poet Robert Burns, called Rab. The degrees are latitude, not heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco's capital lies roughly 34 degrees north of the Equator, so it is a place at that latitude.

clue.text: Pair of hands, all fingers and thumbs, grab outside of red mullet?

indicators.note: a pair of letters, the first two, are taken from the word hands
the I and O take hold of the following letters by going round them

parts.note: fingers and thumbs total ten, written 10, which looks like the letters I and O

indicators.note: only the outside letters of the word red are used

explanation.surface: A clumsy pair of hands fumbles to grab a red fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all fingers and thumbs' looks like clumsiness; it means ten, written 10 and read as IO. A mullet is also a fish, which feeds the false scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The mullet, short at the front and long at the back, is an example of a hairstyle, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Channel surfer heads for the esplanade, after more waves

indicators.note: the heads come after the rearranged letters
waves suggests letters rippling around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the heads of the two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A surfer heads for the seafront when the waves get bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel surfer' looks like a sea surfer; it is the device you flick between TV channels with.
explanation.definitionFit: A TV controller lets a viewer hop between stations, the habit known as channel surfing.

clue.text: Escort stand turning where old cars exhibited

parts.note: a beau is a woman's escort or admirer
the lie of a golf ball is how it stands on the ground
a U-turn is a turn, so U stands for turning

explanation.surface: A Ford Escort is turning on a stand at a car show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escort' looks like the Ford car, fitting the motor scene; it is a beau.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hampshire estate houses Britain's National Motor Museum, where vintage vehicles are displayed.

clue.text: Chauvinistic individual when between the sheets

indicators.note: the letters go between, so inside, the word for the sheets

parts.note: between the sheets means in bed
I, the Roman one, stands for an individual
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A sexist man shows his true colours in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauvinist is prejudiced, holding a one-sided view in favour of their own sex or nation.

clue.text: Perhaps antiperspirant commercial features Arcadian spirit

parts.note: an antiperspirant keeps you dry, so dry is an example of what it does
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A TV advert for deodorant shows a spirit from Arcadia.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood nymph of Greek myth is a spirit of the forest, and Arcadia was the idyllic Greek countryside.

clue.text: 'Age varies in controlled accommodation', boss of 50 states

indicators.note: the word for controlled gives accommodation to, so holds, the rearranged letters

parts.note: to run a company is to control it, so ran means controlled

indicators.note: varies says the letters of the word change their order

explanation.surface: A quoted complaint that the ages in sheltered housing differ, credited to a president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'controlled accommodation' looks like supervised housing; it is RAN holding the mixed-up AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortieth US President led the country of fifty states.

clue.text: Plastic label woven into man's clothing

indicators.note: the word for man's clothes, so wraps round, the rearranged letters

parts.note: male means a man's, as in male clothing

indicators.note: woven suggests strands twisted together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plastic label is sewn into a man's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' looks like the material of the label; it is the adjective meaning pliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a material that can be shaped and bent without breaking.

clue.text: Chubby swimmer given 500-1?

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A tubby swimmer is given 500 to 1 odds of winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chubby' looks like plumpness; it means chub-like, as this freshwater fish is related to the chub.
explanation.definitionFit: A small river fish of the carp family, a close cousin of the chub, so a chub-like swimmer.

clue.text: Refuse centre in resort accepts any rubbish

indicators.note: the centre letters take in the following letters
only the central letters of the word resort are used
rubbish signals the letters are poor and must be reworked

explanation.surface: A rubbish centre at a seaside resort accepts any waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like the noun, rubbish; it is the verb. 'centre in' gives SO, which 'accepts' YAN (the anagram of ANY).
explanation.definitionFit: To decline is to turn something down, the same as giving a negative reply.

clue.text: Pretty face to strike gold, marrying shy aristocrat

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, its first letter

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: shy means short of, so the aristocrat loses one letter at its end

parts.note: a toff is a British slang word for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A pretty face strikes it rich by marrying a bashful aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adjective for the face; it is an adverb meaning fairly. 'shy' cuts TOFF to TOF.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, the definition means somewhat or rather, as in 'pretty good'.

clue.text: Formula often backfires, picking out horse

indicators.note: backfires says the hidden letters are read backwards
picking out means selecting a run of letters from inside the two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A betting system often fails when choosing a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'picking out horse' as the definition, but 'picking out' is what signals the hidden letters, so the definition is just 'horse'.
explanation.definitionFit: A young horse, under a year old, is still a horse.

clue.text: Latest outbursts impede scaling of vocalist

indicators.note: the rearranged letters get in the middle of, so impede, the climbing word
scaling means climbing, so in a down clue the short word reads upwards
outbursts suggest the letters burst out into a new order

explanation.surface: The latest outbursts get in the way of a singer running through scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scaling' looks musical, but in a down clue it means climbing, so 'of' is read upwards; 'impede' then puts the reshuffled 'Latest' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer using a high head voice above the natural range can be called by the name of that voice.

clue.text: Roofman perhaps sells back one that's missing

indicators.note: back means the shortened word is read in reverse
missing says the letter for one is taken out

parts.note: to retail goods is to sell them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A roofer sells back a slate he is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who lays slates on roofs is one kind of roofer, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: One comparatively drunk throws up terribly, emptying an amount here

indicators.note: in a down clue, throws up means the word is turned upwards, so reversed

parts.note: the British saying 'as pissed as a newt' compares a drunk to this amphibian

indicators.note: emptying the word terribly leaves only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A drunk is terribly sick, emptying a large amount here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' points at this clue's own number, 20.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue sits at 20 down, so the amount named here is that number.

clue.text: Potter, Whirlwind (taking frame), in lead for a change

indicators.note: the frame letters go in the rearranged letters
the word lead is changed into a new order
only the frame, the outside letters, of the word whirlwind are taken

explanation.surface: A snooker player nicknamed Whirlwind, at the table, changes the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy 'Whirlwind' White is a snooker player, so 'Potter' and 'frame' suggest snooker. 'Potter' is the verb, to dawdle.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to move about aimlessly at a leisurely pace, the same as idling along.

clue.text: Operative runs declining place in south-east

indicators.note: declining means turning down, so the runs letter is rejected

parts.note: operative means working, in operation
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A worker's run-down town in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A commuter town in Surrey, south-east England, is a place in that region.

clue.text: Slip, fall to ground, pass out

indicators.note: out means the pass letters are taken away

parts.note: to collapse is to fall down to the ground
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Someone slips, falls to the ground and faints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass out' reads as fainting; it means take COL out.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief slip is a minor error or failing, as in a slip of memory.

clue.text: Male cook worked here in Italy

indicators.note: worked means the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A male chef worked here in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep Alpine lake in Lombardy, northern Italy, is a place in that country.

clue.text: Steer around tracks, seeking African creature

indicators.note: the ox letters go around the railway letters

parts.note: a steer is a bullock, an ox
RY is the abbreviation for railway, tracks

explanation.surface: Drive round the tracks looking for an African animal on safari.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb, to drive; it is a castrated bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A large straight-horned antelope of African deserts is an example of an African animal.

clue.text: Parrot caged amongst others — name: Kevin

indicators.note: the parrot's letters cage the letters for amongst others

parts.note: the kea is a New Zealand parrot
e.g. (exempli gratia) means for example, amongst others

explanation.surface: A parrot caged with other birds is named Kevin.
explanation.definitionFit: Kevin is the first name of the England footballer and manager, so the surname is clued by it.

clue.text: One unwilling to chase back in games?

definitions.text: One unwilling to chase back in games?

indicators.note: the unwilling word chases, so comes after, the last letter
the back of the word games is its last letter

parts.note: loth means reluctant or unwilling

explanation.surface: A lazy player who will not run back in sports.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: someone who won't chase back in a match shows idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness personified: a lazy player unwilling to run back shows indolence, and the slow tree mammal shares the name.

clue.text: Vocal prompt to errant surgeon treating patient that's put to sleep?

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so the words are taken by how they sound

parts.words: prompt to errant surgeon treating patient
parts.note: a nurse would remind a surgeon about to operate on the wrong part: hip, not eyes

explanation.surface: A shouted warning to a surgeon about to operate on the wrong part of an anaesthetised patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put to sleep' suggests anaesthetic; the question mark flags that trance, not anaesthesia, is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Inducing a trance is likened to putting someone to sleep, hence the question mark.
